encoding_guidelines_findings: This is the haftarah blessing, not a Bible verse. Keep the single prayer-part milestone (…/asher_bachar/text) and its terminator. Do not add verse or half-verse milestones and do not cite chapter and verse. The half-verse rule ('from the accents, mechanically') applies to Tanakh verses only, so even an etnachta here creates no /a or /b URN.
When accents are added, the te'amim on יְיָ must stay inside j:divineName together with its vowels.

Unicode: silluq and meteg share U+05BD. Record which is meant in review notes, not in the text. Pashta is U+0599 after the final letter. If a stress-position pashta is confirmed, encode it as a second U+0599 on its letter rather than substituting qadma (U+05A8).

The printed final mark is a large colon. Keep it as in current.json (ASCII ':', consistent with the project) unless the project convention for accented text says U+05C3. Don't change it here unilaterally.
No tei:sic/corr is needed. The missing accents are a transcription omission, not a misprint in the source. The English (s175) is unaffected, and no English was invented.
limits: Resolution limits most of the sublinear reading. Many printed strokes are present, but I can't name them reliably. The transcription string deliberately leaves them out, so it is incomplete relative to the print. It is not a full accent text.

I did not read the original independent-174.json directly because it was not at the path I tried. The comparison relies on 03/review.json, which quotes it as recognizing te'amim without transcribing them. My readings agree with 03 on the mahpakh under אֲשֶׁר and הַבּוֹחֵר, the pashta on בָּחַר and בַּתּוֹרָה, the zaqef on הָעוֹלָם, טוֹבִים and עַבְדּוֹ, and the silluq on וָצֶדֶק. I don't confirm 03's zaqef on עַמּוֹ.
